thread:
Sam (PM): Heads-up from customer calls: three asks touching private deployments: smaller offline installers, safer delta upgrades, and explicit egress-preservation runbooks. need to decide sprint scope.
Tariq (Eng): Can we short-list must-haves?
Sam (PM): Must: 1) installer tarball with sha256 and --dry-run, 2) pre-upgrade preflight + snapshot for quick revert, 3) field runbook for preserving egress IPs. Nice-to-have: automated NAT translation.
Jo (Field Eng): ACME wants the installer to accept preloaded images and write a minimal /var/log/rw-install.log. Their team has slow disks and strict change windows.
Priya (SRE): Preflight should catch CNI mismatches, kernel params, and disk pressure. Revert must avoid full DB restores in common failure modes.
Hana (CS): BetaCorp will accept a manual NAT procedure in v1 if we deliver clear runbook and validation artifact. They asked for an SLA window for upgrades.
Tariq (Eng): Dev notes: compact bundle + preloaded image flow is low risk. Egress automation depends on CNI; we can document supported CNIs and manual steps for others.
Sam (PM): Proposal: sprint split: focus on compact/offline installer + preflight/revert. Deliver a v1 runbook for egress and schedule automation for sprint+1.
Jo (Field Eng): Launch gates: 1) offline install passes on 2-node slow-disk lab, 2) installer < 1GB added, 3) runbook draft uploaded. I can validate tests.
Priya (SRE): Upgrade gates: 1) preflight detects critical mismatches, 2) snapshot & revert restores service order, 3) telemetry event for "preflight-failure".
Tariq (Eng): Estimates: spike 2pts, installer work 3pts, preflight+revert 3pts, docs/tests 1pt. Two devs OK.
Sam (PM): Actions: Tariq open spike PR EOW, Jo run lab Thurs, Priya draft preflight checklist, Hana confirm BetaCorp window. reconvene Friday 10:00 to lock scope.
